practices.practice: Create a single MongoClient and reuse it for the lifetime of the process (singleton client pattern); do not instantiate a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single global MongoClient and reuse it for the lifetime of the process; do not instantiate a new client per request. Tune pool sizes (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) in the URI/options for expected concurrency.

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS enabled (tls=true) and validate server certificates in production; Azure DocumentDB requires TLS.
practices.prior_belief: Always connect with TLS/SSL enabled (e.g., include tls=true or ssl=true in the MongoDB URI) and validate server certificates unless explicitly using a trusted internal test endpoint.

practices.practice: Implement retries for transient errors (e.g., 429, 503, network timeouts) with exponential backoff and jitter; rely on the driver's retryable-reads when available and respect Retry-After when provided.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors (HTTP 429, 503, network timeouts); respect Retry-After if returned by the server.

practices.practice: Store vectors as a JSON numeric array (number[]) in the document field so they can be indexed by cosmosSearch; non-number types (or unsupported encodings) may prevent a document from being indexed.
practices.prior_belief: Store vector embeddings as a fixed-length float32 array with an explicit binary BSON subtype (use the provider-supported subtype, e.g., 0x09 if the server expects it), and record the embedding dimension in the document schema to validate clients (e.g., {embeddingDim:512}).

practices.practice: If you use cosine similarity, L2-normalize embeddings at encode time (and store model+dimension metadata with vectors) so queries use the same normalization and the index returns consistent similarity scores.
practices.prior_belief: L2-normalize embeddings on the client (or store both normalized and raw) if you plan to use cosine similarity in the index, or ensure the index/index option explicitly selects the appropriate similarity (cosine vs. inner-product vs. L2).
practices.source_name: documentdb-vector-search

practices.practice: Choose an index type that matches your scale (vector-ivf / vector-hnsw / vector-diskann) and configure algorithm parameters (dimensions, numLists/nProbes for IVF or m/efConstruction/efSearch for HNSW) rather than relying on defaults.
practices.prior_belief: When creating a vector index prefer an approximate index (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN) tuned for your workload: specify dimensions (512), index type (vector-ivf or hnsw), and index-specific parameters (e.g., nlist or ncentroids for IVF; M/efConstruction for HNSW) rather than using a default generic index.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Create vector/search indexes before bulk-loading production data and wait (or use the blocking option) for the index build to complete; track build progress with db.currentOp/listIndexes before running heavy queries.
practices.prior_belief: Build vector indexes before bulk-loading production datasets and wait for the index build to complete (check listIndexes or server index status) — do not run heavy vector queries while index builds are in progress.
practices.source_name: Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB createIndexes and tracking index build status

practices.practice: For bulk ingestion use batched writes (insert_many / bulk_write) with unordered writes (ordered=false) and tuned batch sizes (client guidance ~500–1000 per batch or use SDK bulk modes) instead of per-document inserts.
practices.prior_belief: For bulk seeding use insert_many or bulk_write with ordered=False and reasonably sized batches (e.g., 500–5000 docs) to avoid memory/timeouts; avoid one-document inserts in loops.
practices.source_name: Tips for optimizing vector indexing & search performance
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search performance tips: bulk ingestion

practices.practice: Do not return full embedding vectors in API responses by default; return only metadata and a score unless clients explicitly need the raw embedding.
practices.prior_belief: Do not return the full embedding vector in API responses by default; project only required metadata and a score to minimize bandwidth and avoid leaking model outputs.
practices.how_found: embeddings API response do not return embeddings best practice

practices.practice: Put the $search aggregation stage first in any aggregation pipeline that uses DocumentDB search (including cosmosSearch vector queries); the search index narrows candidate set before other stages.
practices.prior_belief: Put the $search (or provider vector-search) stage as the first stage in any aggregation pipeline if using a provider search aggregation API; many engines require the search stage to be first to produce relevance-ordered results.
practices.source_name: Full-text search in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: $search must be the first stage guidance

practices.practice: When issuing a vector similarity query include a server-side top-k limit (k) and use the index scoring (searchScore) so the engine returns the top-k ordered by similarity instead of sorting client-side.
practices.prior_belief: When issuing a vector similarity query request, include a top-k limit (e.g., limit: 8) and use server-side scoring to return results in descending similarity order instead of sorting client-side.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Prefer the provider's native vector-search operator (cosmosSearch via $search) for kNN retrieval rather than brute-force client-side distance computations.
practices.prior_belief: If the provider supports it, prefer using a dedicated vector-search API/operator (e.g., a vendor-provided $search with vector clause) rather than brute-force client-side distance computation for performance and accuracy.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Tune cluster/collection throughput (cluster tier or autoscale) to account for vector indexing and query costs; monitor resource consumption (CPU, memory, IOPS) and scale up or enable autoscale for ingestion/indexing bursts.
practices.prior_belief: Tune collection/cluster throughput (RUs or instance tier) to account for the cost of vector queries and index build operations; use autoscale or provisioned capacity and monitor consumed throughput during indexing and queries.
practices.source_name: Tips for optimizing vector indexing & search performance

practices.practice: For local development and CI keep credentials out of logs and repository files; provide a .env.example and drive connection settings from environment variables or Key Vault references.
practices.prior_belief: For development and CI, keep credentials out of logs and sample data; provide a .env.example with placeholders and document how to set DOCUMENTDB_URI rather than providing real URIs in repository files.

practices.practice: Measure approximate-index recall by comparing index results to brute-force (small validation set) and adjust index/query parameters (nProbes, efSearch, oversampling) if recall is insufficient.
practices.prior_belief: Measure and compare approximate index recall by computing brute-force (CPU) top-K on a small validation set and compare to index results; adjust index params (nprobe, ef) if recall is too low.
practices.source_name: documentdb-vector-search

practices.practice: Prefer storing vectors as arrays of numeric values (float32/float16) in fields and use the documented vector-field encodings/options (float types, half/quantization) rather than relying on an undocumented BSON binary packing; verify encoding support in the service docs before using a binary subtype.
practices.prior_belief: When packing embeddings into BSON binary ensure byte order and type match server expectations (float32 little-endian); use a consistent serializer (e.g., numpy.astype('float32').tobytes()) and validate roundtrip reads in tests.

practices.practice: Avoid storing large images or binary blobs inside DocumentDB documents; store image blobs in Azure Blob Storage and keep only URLs/metadata/embeddings in the database.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid embedding large images/large blobs in the DB documents; store image URLs or use a dedicated blob store and index metadata/embeddings in DocumentDB only.
practices.source_name: Optimize storage cost in Azure Cosmos DB (recommend storing media in Blob Storage)
practices.how_found: store images in blob storage best practice

practices.practice: Capture server error payloads and inspect query plans (explain / currentOp); use explain/profile/diagnostic logs to troubleshoot vector-query failures and index usage.
practices.prior_belief: Log and capture server error payloads and query plans (explain) when a vector query fails; use the DB provider's explain or profile tools to diagnose requirements like whether $search must be the initial pipeline stage.
practices.source_name: Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Protect the database at the network level (IP firewall rules, Private Endpoint/VNet) and use least-privilege credentials or Microsoft Entra authentication / RBAC instead of long-lived cluster admin keys.
practices.prior_belief: Protect the database at network level (IP firewall rules, private endpoints or VNet) and restrict the credentials to least privilege (database user scoped to sample_retail_11 rather than cluster admin).
practices.source_name: documentdb-security

practices.practice: When creating an IVF vector index set numLists appropriately (e.g., ~documentCount/1000 for up to 1M docs; increase numLists as dataset grows) and tune nProbes/efSearch at query time to trade recall vs latency.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB (IVF guidance)

practices.practice: For HNSW tune m and efConstruction at index-build time and efSearch at query time (higher values improve recall but increase build time / memory or query latency); consider DiskANN for very large corpora.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB (HNSW / DiskANN guidance)

practices.practice: Project the similarity score from $search using { score: { $meta: 'searchScore' } } in a downstream $project stage to return relevance scores with documents.

practices.practice: Wait until a search/index reports status READY/queryable (via $listSearchIndexes or listIndexes/getIndexes) before running production queries that depend on it.

notes: I inspected the sample app and the installed DocumentDB skills, and searched Microsoft documentation for Azure DocumentDB vector-search and related guidance. Most prior beliefs K01..K04, K06..K09, K11..K16, K18..K20 were confirmed by Azure DocumentDB public documentation or the installed DocumentDB skills. Two prior beliefs were contradicted by the public record for Azure DocumentDB: K05 (the public docs require numeric arrays for vectors / documented encodings rather than an undocumented BSON binary subtype) and K17 (there is no public guidance endorsing arbitrary BSON binary float32 packing; the public docs emphasize vector arrays and documented encodings). K10 (do not return embeddings in API responses) had no Azure DocumentDB public documentation explicitly addressing it, so it is recorded as prior_knowledge_only with the searches attempted.
